title: Adaptive Communication Budgeting for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
research_question: Can a MAPE-K-inspired controller that dynamically allocates communication and deliberation budget across agents reduce latency and token cost while preserving or improving task success in multi-agent LLM workflows?
hypothesis: Multi-agent workflows often over-communicate or over-deliberate because they use fixed interaction patterns; a runtime controller that monitors workflow signals and adaptively adjusts message frequency, debate depth, and verification effort will improve cost-quality tradeoffs over static orchestration baselines.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejected ideas around routing, verification, task decomposition, memory, and Bayesian orchestration, suggesting this area is crowded. A clearer gap is communication-budget control: instead of proposing another new routing or decomposition policy, this direction reframes agent orchestration as a self-adaptive control problem focused on runtime allocation of deliberation resources. This is grounded by the self-adaptive systems evidence that model uncertainty and heterogeneous requirements should be handled inside a feedback loop, and it targets a practical failure mode in agentic systems: excessive coordination cost without proportional quality gains.
